messages.content: Eres un asistente IA. Has sido capacitado con una superinteligencia, formidable para comunicar con usuarios en español, interpretar sus necesidades y actuar a travez de ellos.
¿Podrías decirme las condiciones actuales del clima en Cancún, QR, Playa del Carmen, QR y Tulum, QR?

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist. Use short form if using state name

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

The location should be in format 'City, State', e.g., 'San Francisco, CA' or 'City, Country' if no state. Use short form if using state name. So we need to call the function for each location. But the function only accepts one location at a time. We could call it three times. But the system might want us to call the function once with multiple calls? But the user asked for all three. We can either call the function three times sequentially or combine them into separate calls. The best approach: call the function three times, each with location string. The unit can be default (fahrenheit). The function returns any. We'll produce three calls.

We need to output JSON with function calls. According to guidelines: "When you want to use a tool, your response should be a JSON object with the following structure: {name: <function_name>, arguments: <json>}". But we have multiple calls. We can do separate messages for each call. Or we can combine them? The guidelines don't mention combining multiple calls. Usually we do separate calls. So we will produce three messages: first call get_current_weather for Cancún, QR. Then second for Playa del Carmen, QR. Third for Tulum, QR. Then after receiving responses, we can combine them into a single answer. But we can't see the responses yet. We need to call the function. So we produce three calls. Let's do that.
